title: Processing of identified data during registration
description: During account registration, the Homeowner provides identified personal data (name, email, contact information) which is processed by the Home Hub. This creates a direct link between the data subject and their personal information.
assumptions: Registration requires personal identification information

title: Unique identifiers in device enrollment
description: Camera and sensor enrollment involves unique device identifiers that can be linked back to the Homeowner's account, creating persistent identifiers for tracking and identification.
assumptions: Devices have unique serial numbers or IDs that are registered

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: The Home Hub can link all registered devices and account data through unique identifiers (account ID, device IDs), enabling comprehensive linking of the Homeowner's data across the system.
assumptions: System maintains identifier-based relationships between account and devices

title: Profiling through device enrollment patterns
description: The combination of account registration data and enrolled device types/locations can be analyzed to profile the Homeowner's lifestyle, security preferences, and home characteristics.
assumptions: Device enrollment data includes device types and potentially location information

title: Potentially excessive data sensitivity in registration
description: Account registration may collect more sensitive personal data than functionally required for basic device enrollment, such as detailed contact information or identity verification data.
assumptions: Registration form may request data beyond minimum necessary for functionality
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific registration requirements not fully specified

title: Data retention during registration process
description: Personal data collected during registration and device enrollment may be retained longer than functionally necessary, especially if no clear data lifecycle management is implemented.
assumptions: System retains registration data indefinitely without clear retention policy
uncertainty_note: Retention policy not specified in flow description

title: Unawareness of data processing scope
description: Homeowner may not be fully aware of all personal data being collected, how it will be processed, or what third parties may have access during the registration and enrollment process.
assumptions: Privacy notices may not clearly explain all data processing activities

title: Limited control over data processing preferences
description: During registration, the Homeowner may have limited ability to set preferences or provide granular consent for how their personal data and device information will be processed.
assumptions: Registration process may use blanket consent rather than granular preferences

title: Attributable registration data
description: Registration and device enrollment creates data records that can be attributed to the specific Homeowner, preventing them from denying these actions were taken.
assumptions: System maintains logs and records of registration activities

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: If the registration process collects more personal data than necessary for device enrollment functionality, this could violate GDPR's data minimization principle.
assumptions: Registration may collect data beyond functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific data collection practices not fully detailed

title: Access code and entry data retained longer than necessary
description: The Home Hub may store the temporary access code, timestamp, and access event data longer than functionally required for the door unlocking operation. Without clear retention policies, this data could be kept indefinitely.
assumptions: System logs access events and stores them for audit or security purposes

title: Collection of potentially sensitive access data
description: The Home Hub collects access code entries which, while temporary, could be considered sensitive authentication data. If combined with timestamps and location data, this creates a record of guest presence and movement.
assumptions: System records access attempts with associated metadata

title: Guest unaware of data collection during access
description: The guest entering the temporary access code may not be aware that their access attempt, timing, and potentially other metadata are being collected and stored by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: No clear notification or consent mechanism exists for data collection

title: Guest lacks control over access data processing
description: The guest has no ability to set preferences or provide consent regarding how their access data is collected, stored, or used by the Home Hub system.
assumptions: No user interface or mechanism for guest data preferences

title: Access events create attributable data evidence
description: The Home Hub creates data records of access code entries that can be used to attribute the door unlocking action to a specific guest at a specific time, preventing the guest from denying the access event.
assumptions: System maintains logs of access attempts with timestamps

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: The Home Hub may collect and store more data than necessary for the door unlocking function (e.g., detailed timestamps, multiple access attempts, guest identifiers) without clear justification.
assumptions: System collects metadata beyond what's strictly needed for access control
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual system implementation and data retention policies

title: Profiling through video analysis
description: Video clips uploaded from the Home Hub can be analyzed to profile individuals based on their activities, movements, and behaviors captured in the footage.
assumptions: Video content contains identifiable individuals and their activities

title: Linking through unique identifiers
description: Video clips may contain unique identifiers (device IDs, user IDs, timestamps) that enable linking data across the cloud storage system and potentially with other data sources.
assumptions: Video metadata or content includes unique identifiers

title: Processing of identified data
description: The Home Hub processes video clips that contain identified information such as faces, license plates, and other personally identifiable visual data.
assumptions: Video clips capture identifiable individuals and objects

title: Revealing attributes in stored video
description: Stored video clips contain revealing attributes (location, time, people, activities) that support identification of data subjects.
assumptions: Video content reveals identifying attributes

title: Video as attributable evidence
description: Video clips can be used as data evidence to attribute actions or presence to specific individuals, preventing them from denying certain claims.
assumptions: Video content can identify individuals and their actions

title: Sensitive video data collection
description: Video clips are highly sensitive personal data that may be more sensitive than functionally required, especially if recording areas beyond what's necessary for security purposes.
assumptions: Video may capture more than functionally needed

title: Extended video retention
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage may be retained longer than functionally needed, increasing privacy risks over time.
assumptions: Retention policies may exceed functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific retention policy configuration

title: Third-party cloud provider access
description: Personal video data is made accessible to cloud storage provider as a predetermined party, which may exceed what's functionally necessary.
assumptions: Cloud provider has access to stored video data

title: Unawareness of video recording and storage
description: Data subjects captured in video clips may be unaware that their personal data is being collected, processed, and stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: People in video may not know they're being recorded

title: Limited control over video deletion
description: Data subjects may lack control to rectify or erase their personal data from video clips stored in cloud storage.
assumptions: Video deletion mechanisms may be limited or complex

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: Storing all recorded video clips may violate the data minimization principle if more data is processed than actually needed for the security function.
assumptions: All video clips are stored regardless of necessity
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific system configuration and retention policies

title: Storage limitation principle violation
description: Video clips may be stored longer than needed for the stated purpose, violating the storage limitation principle.
assumptions: Retention period exceeds functional requirements
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific retention policy configuration

title: Motion alert contains device/user identifier
description: The motion alert forwarded from the Home Hub likely contains a device identifier or user account ID that uniquely references the data subject, enabling identification of who owns the home hub.
assumptions: Motion alerts typically include device or account identifiers for routing and authentication purposes

title: Motion data reveals revealing attributes
description: Motion alert data reveals when movement occurs in the home, which can indicate occupancy patterns, daily routines, and presence/absence of individuals.
assumptions: Motion sensors detect movement that correlates with human activity in the home

title: Motion patterns enable individual profiling
description: Real-time motion alerts can be analyzed to create behavioral profiles of individuals, revealing patterns such as sleep schedules, work hours, and daily routines.
assumptions: Motion data over time can be aggregated and analyzed for behavioral patterns

title: Motion data is sensitive personal data
description: Motion alert data is sensitive as it reveals occupancy and movement patterns in a private residence, which should only be collected when strictly required.
assumptions: Motion data in a home context is considered sensitive personal data

title: Implicit disclosure of occupancy patterns
description: Motion alerts implicitly disclose when the home is occupied or vacant, revealing personal information beyond the explicit purpose of the alert.
assumptions: Motion detection inherently reveals presence/absence information

title: Data subjects unaware of motion data processing
description: Individuals in the home may not be aware that their motion data is being collected and transmitted to the mobile app backend in real-time.
assumptions: Motion sensors may operate without explicit notification to all data subjects

title: Lack of control over motion data preferences
description: Data subjects may lack control to set preferences about when motion data is collected, how frequently it's transmitted, or whether it's shared with the backend.
assumptions: Home hub systems may not provide granular privacy controls for motion data

title: Potential violation of data minimization principle
description: Real-time motion alerts may process more personal data than functionally necessary, especially if historical motion data is retained beyond what's needed for the alert functionality.
assumptions: GDPR data minimization principle applies to motion data processing
uncertainty_note: Depends on specific retention policies and functional requirements

title: Profiling through motion detection patterns
description: Motion detection notifications can reveal patterns about when the homeowner is present or absent from their property. Over time, this data can be analyzed to profile the homeowner's daily routines, travel patterns, and occupancy habits.
assumptions: The backend stores or processes motion detection events that can be correlated over time

title: Processing of identified homeowner data
description: The mobile app backend processes identified data to route motion detection notifications to the specific homeowner's device. This requires maintaining and using personal identifiers.
assumptions: The system uses personal identifiers to deliver notifications to the correct user

title: Detection through observed communications
description: The notification communications themselves reveal that motion detection is active and when motion events occur. An observer monitoring communications could detect these patterns.
assumptions: Communication channels could be monitored by third parties

title: Sensitive motion data disclosure
description: Motion detection data is sensitive as it reveals occupancy patterns and when the property is vacant. This information could be misused for burglary planning or other malicious purposes.
assumptions: Motion detection data is considered sensitive personal data in this context

title: Excessive notification frequency
description: If motion detection notifications are sent too frequently (e.g., for every minor motion event), this could constitute excessive processing of personal data beyond what is functionally needed.
assumptions: The system may not have adequate filtering or aggregation of motion events
uncertainty_note: Depends on system configuration and notification settings

title: Lack of notification preference control
description: The homeowner may lack sufficient control over notification preferences, such as frequency, timing, or types of motion events that trigger notifications.
assumptions: The system may not provide granular notification controls to users

title: Potential data minimization violation
description: If notifications include more information than necessary (e.g., exact timestamps, location details, or motion intensity) beyond what the homeowner needs to know, this could violate data minimization principles.
assumptions: The notification content may include unnecessary details
uncertainty_note: Depends on actual notification content design

title: Sensitive video data stored in cloud
description: Video clips stored in cloud storage contain highly sensitive personal data including visual recordings of the homeowner's property and potentially people, activities, and private moments. This data type is inherently sensitive and requires strict protection.
assumptions: Video content may capture identifiable individuals, property details, and private activities

title: Video retention duration unclear
description: Personal video data may be stored longer than functionally needed for playback purposes. Without clear retention policies, video clips could be kept indefinitely, increasing privacy risk.
assumptions: Storage duration policies may not be clearly defined or enforced

title: Processing of identified video data
description: The mobile app backend processes video clips that may contain identified information such as faces, license plates, or other personally identifiable visual data during retrieval for playback.
assumptions: Video content may contain identifiable individuals or objects

title: Video metadata contains unique identifiers
description: Video files may contain metadata with unique references to the homeowner identity, such as account IDs, device identifiers, or timestamps that can identify the data subject.
assumptions: Video metadata includes identifying information linked to homeowner account

title: Profiling through video playback patterns
description: Analysis of video retrieval and playback patterns could be used to profile homeowner behavior, routines, and presence patterns at their property.
assumptions: Playback metadata and timing could be analyzed for behavioral patterns

title: Video data as attributable evidence
description: Retrieved video clips can be used as data evidence to attribute events or activities to the homeowner, potentially preventing them from denying certain claims about their property or activities.
assumptions: Video content can serve as evidentiary material

title: Limited homeowner control over video processing
description: Homeowners may lack control over how their video data is processed, including preferences for retention, access, and deletion of stored video clips.
assumptions: User interface may not provide comprehensive data control options

title: Potential violation of data minimization
description: Retrieving and processing full video clips may involve more personal data than strictly necessary for the playback functionality, potentially violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Full video retrieval may be required for playback but could be optimized
